routing_warnings.description: The USB-powered load-transient collapse, low DCDC1 output, and DCDC1 degradation belong to the independently tracked DCDC1 regulation Requirement; only the concrete battery-only source-path success is retained here.

The new information in this message concerns the suspected AXP2101 exposed-pad soldering and windowpane paste aperture; its voltage-failure observation duplicates message 989 for the target Requirement.
The zero-voltage observation concerns USB-powered operation of the later integrated AXP2101 board, not the modular main-board LDO.
The integrated board's 3.3V rail starts successfully; the concrete failure reported here is native USB enumeration.
The USB-powered rail-collapse observations concern AXP2101 DCDC1 on the integrated board rather than the modular standalone LDO.
The unsuccessful AXP2101 replacement concerns the persistent integrated-board DCDC1 problem.
The abnormal L3 voltage is direct execution evidence for DCDC1 regulation; this source does not identify the thermal-pad assembly as its cause.
The factory voltage failure belongs to DCDC1 regulation, while the proposed thermal-pad paste explanation remains speculative in this source.
The reported L3 short is a DCDC1 failure, and the X-ray inspection found no evidence of poor AXP2101 welding.
The load-transient collapse and leaking DCDC1 output are execution evidence for regulation stability rather than thermal-pad assembly.
Persistent malfunction after an attempted AXP2101 replacement concerns DCDC1 operation; improper replacement soldering is only speculative.
The incorrectly grounded U3 VBUS pin is a defect in the USB ESD-protection circuit; the resulting enumeration failure is already represented under the target Requirement.
The proposed change to route U3 pin 5 to VBUS concerns the ESD-protection circuit rather than a change to native USB behavior.
The requested separation of U3 VBUS and GND while retaining D+/D- pass-through directly modifies the USB ESD-protection Requirement.
The observed failure to enumerate is direct execution evidence for native USB operation; it is used here only as supporting context for the identified ESD wiring defect.
Removing U3 and bridging the data lines restored USB operation, verifying the native USB path while leaving the ESD-protection Requirement unsatisfied.
Enumeration and flashing after removing U3 and bridging the data lines verify native USB operation without verifying the required ESD protection.
The message concerns retention of existing signal-to-GPIO assignments rather than module selection or breakout design.
The proposed 5V_EN GPIO reassignment belongs to GPIO assignment compatibility.
The concrete USB enumeration and flashing success belongs to the native USB Requirement, not the module-breakout Requirement.
The load-transient collapses and external-3.3V comparison concern DCDC1 regulation rather than module selection or pin breakout.
The PIR and touch resistor question concerns sensor-input biasing rather than the active-low mechanical panel controls.
Item 3 independently confirms pull-down behavior for PIR and touch inputs and should be routed to the sensor-input-biasing Requirement.
The reported hard resets are explicitly caused by DCDC1 rail collapse under load, not by the BOOT/reset circuit.
The requested adjacency and orientation of the battery and board connectors concern power-board physical placement.
The INA219 shunt placement and downstream-current measurement path are more specifically owned by the rail-current-monitoring Requirement.
Top-edge placement and physical alignment of connectors across the main and sensor boards are mechanical-layout constraints.
The connectors are reported missing from the manufacturing parts list rather than from the electrical PCB design.
This reports that the main-board connectors became unavailable in stock.
The client accepts adding the previously omitted connector parts to the manufacturing order configuration.
This message removes the optional sensor level-shifter provision rather than changing the connector inventory.
The requirement to hardwire the SPS30 SEL input to ground belongs to the independently tracked SPS30 mode-selection behavior.
Moving bottom connectors upward and changing their orientation is a sensor-board mechanical-layout requirement.
In context, the missing sensor-board connectors concern parts availability and manufacturer ordering rather than absence of the required interfaces from the design.
The level-shifter clause concerns LED power and data-level compatibility; only the LED-package clause belongs to the target Requirement.
Separate LED power control and level-shifter necessity concern the LED electrical interface rather than the physical indicator board.
The change to 3.3V LED power and removal of the level shifter belongs to the LED power-and-logic Requirement.
The requested I2C connector is for an independently addable ambient-light sensor, not the backlight driver circuit.
The updated document adds the ambient-light sensor I2C interface rather than changing the backlight driver.
The request to place the battery JST beside the board JST primarily concerns battery-connector placement.
The accepted spacing and mounting-hole clearance condition concerns the proposed battery and board connector arrangement.
The reported inability to fit the connectors within 40 mm concerns the battery-connector placement trajectory.
Moving the battery connector opposite the USB-C connector directly changes battery-connector placement.
The flexible power-pin order and matching main-board connector concern the electrical interboard interface rather than mechanical layout.
The requested panel power-button connector defines the panel power-control behavior rather than a general power-board layout change.
The claim about implemented AXP2101 cooling belongs to the dedicated thermal-pad assembly Requirement.
The corrected USBLC6 pin wiring concerns USB ESD protection rather than mechanical layout.
The claim that all components are on the board follows the sensor-board layout discussion and does not unambiguously refer to the main board.
The J_BAT short-edge clause specifically changes the independently tracked battery-connector placement Requirement; the other mechanical constraints remain under the target Requirement.
The reported enclosure obstruction specifically concerns access to the battery connector above USB, not the integrated layout as a whole.
The proposed revision corefers to the battery-connector obstruction discussed in message 860.
The client's approval verifies the revised battery-connector placement only, not the complete integrated-board layout.
Missing LCSC part numbers and questions about unexpected BOM entries concern BOM correctness rather than component sourceability alone.
The reported JLCPCB rotation issue concerns assembly component orientation.
Failure to access the manufacturer's account through an invitation concerns order setup assistance.
Whether optional connectors remain in the BOM concerns BOM contents and DNP handling, not evidence that the connectors are sourceable.
The observed AXP2101 load-transient collapse primarily concerns stable DCDC1 regulation rather than the sourceability constraint.
The complaint about numerous JLCPCB extended components and setup fees primarily concerns component sourceability and cost rather than BOM completeness.
The component replacements address unavailable parts and are more specifically owned by the component-sourceability Requirement.
The observed AXP2101 soldering-yield problem concerns thermal-pad assembly rather than BOM correctness.
The explicitly observed defect is an incomplete BOM; the accompanying positions-file request does not establish a distinct production-package transition.
The missing machine-local 3D models and broken library paths concern editable KiCad project portability, not manufacturing exports.
The concern about unnecessary JLCPCB extended-component fees primarily changes the component-sourceability constraint.
The reported incorrect component rotations concern assembly orientation rather than account or basket setup.
The request is specifically to review component orientations in JLCPCB.
The request seeks a less expensive, more sourceable connector alternative.
The freelancer claims to have selected a replacement component; this concerns component sourceability.
The client verifies that the proposed replacement retains the same high price and minimum order.
Checking whether BOM items are JLCPCB basic components primarily concerns component sourceability.
The client specifically requests verification of component orientation.
The message requests a complete BOM and component-position data for a quote.
The reported assembly-yield issue concerns the AXP2101 thermal-pad paste aperture.
The anticipated enclosure obstruction concerns battery-connector placement on the integrated PCB rather than an observed failure or change of the enclosure Requirement.
The acceptance also applies to the third NTC-terminal proposal in message 12 and should independently introduce battery temperature sensing.
The clause requiring an NTC connection at J_BAT belongs to the separate battery-temperature-sensing Requirement.
The freelancer's thermal-protection clarification concerns battery temperature sensing rather than the target electrical-protection behavior.
The three-pin JST-PH connector and GND/VCC/NTC pin definition belong to the battery connector interface.
The enclosure obstruction concerns battery connector placement and accessibility.
The accepted 2.5A battery-trace capacity concerns high-current PCB routing rather than the battery protection circuit.
The message specifies the battery connector type, pin count, and GND/VCC/NTC pin interface rather than changing the temperature-sensing behavior.
The reported labeling problem concerns the battery connector pinout and does not demonstrate failure of battery temperature sensing.
The L-shaped connector orientation concerns physical placement and accessibility rather than the electrical interface.
The reported inability to plug in the battery concerns connector clearance.
Placing the battery connector beside the board connector is a mechanical-layout requirement.
Hole clearance and spacing between connectors concern mechanical placement.
Placing the battery connector opposite USB-C concerns physical layout.
Requiring J_BAT on a short edge concerns integrated-board connector placement.
The enclosure blocking access to the battery connector is a concrete placement and accessibility failure.
In context, this proposes a revised battery-connector location, but the source alone is too generic for an implementation Event.
The client approves the revised battery-connector placement after the enclosure-clearance issue.
The standby-current observation concerns independently controlled LED power cutoff rather than supply-voltage or data-level compatibility.
The proposal to cut the LED rail when unused belongs to the dedicated standby-power switching Requirement.
The proposed transistor cutoff addresses LED standby draw.
The statement describes switched LED power behavior and should be considered under the dedicated standby-switching Requirement.
The separate LED-versus-sensor power-control clause also affects the dedicated LED standby-switching Requirement.
The selected LED package and part number belong to the physical eight-LED board Requirement.
The N-channel and P-channel MOSFET combination concerns switching the 3.3V LED supply.
The connector pin-mapping concern belongs to the LED board interface and pinout Requirement.
The correction identifying LED connector pin 1 as 3.3V belongs to the LED board pinout.
This message changes the LED supply voltage and data-level compatibility; it does not independently establish the standby switching behavior.
The question concerns control of the boost-converter enable pin, which belongs to the switched 5V sensor rail rather than ESP32 sleep/wake behavior.
The boost converter's default-off behavior concerns the GPIO-switched 5V sensor rail.
The local-input-decoupling question concerns the AXP2101 DCDC1 VIN path, not the ESP32 module's local 3V3 decoupling.
In context, the freelancer's decoupling-capacitor claim answers the DCDC1 VIN decoupling question rather than the ESP32 local-capacitor placement.
The capacitors near the USB connector concern power-input decoupling, not ESP32-local 3V3 decoupling.

missing_requirement_candidates.description: The client independently requires maximizing battery operating life, which is broader than source selection and charge-while-operating behavior and has no clear target in the frozen inventory.
The requested placement of a local 0.1 µF capacitor within 2 mm of the ESP32 3V3 pin is an independently targetable power-integrity constraint not covered by the module-and-breakout boundary.

The client specifies operating frequencies, automatic light sleep, deep-sleep conditions, and timer and touch-button wake sources; this independently evolving power-management behavior does not fit the GPIO-assignment Requirement.
The client independently requests and proceeds with replacing the modular multi-board architecture with one integrated board; the target Requirement explicitly excludes this architectural decision.

The client adds a missing JST-GH connector to the integrated design, but the connector's function is unavailable in the supplied text, so it cannot be safely mapped to an existing interface Requirement.

The evidence contains separate power-board, sensor-board, and main/integrated-board BOM failure and verification paths. Global audit should assess whether REQ_ASSEMBLY_READY_BOM is under-split by board context.
